title: Fact-checking Chilton: Ben Webster, Charlie Echols and the Famous Door
summary: Willard checks Chilton details against Lee, including Albuquerque, Ben Webster's months with the band, Don Byas with Charlie Echols in 1936, and the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Back to Ben, you mentioned also that you met him in Albuquerque, and in the Chilton book, under Ben's name, it says that he joined the Young Family Campbell Kirkie Band in Campbellquerque, New Mexico and toured with the band for 3 months, is that right?
Campbell Kirkie? Campbellquerque?
Cam -- it says, hey, he must mean ...
He means Albuquerque.
He must not have understood what Campbell Kirkie somebody had said, because he wrote Campbellquerque, and that doesn't sound right.
I don't think there's such a place. It's Albuquerque.
I - I didn't say it out loud though.
It was Albuquerque.
Yeah. Okay. And he toured with your band for a few months.
Uh huh. Yes, he has those facts right. Yeah.
That's funny. If I hadn't said it out loud ...
Campbell Kirkie Campbellquerque.
Right.
Two words.
Yeah.
When you were with Charlie Echols, was it the same time that Don Byas was with Charlie Echols?
Uh huh, yeah -- I think so.
Well, then that was 1936 according to Chilton again.
Right.
And when you were talking about The Famous Door on Vine Street, you started out talking about the Brown Derby, and ...
No, I got them mixed up.
Okay, I just wanted to get that straight.
No, no. I didn't mean the Brown Derby, no.
So you didn't mean the Brown Derby; you meant The Famous Door
No, I thought I did that. No, they never did, no. It was The Famous Door.
